prompt: The September Declaration has a rough equivalent in the Netherlands that takes place on the same day every year. In what century was the current name of this day (as of August 2024) chosen?
answer: The current use of the name **Prinsjesdag** for the annual opening of Parliament dates to the **19th century**, with references appearing by the late 1800s. (The name itself originally referred to celebrations of William V’s birthday in the 18th century.)
